newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's slow recovery clouds steelmakers profits.
newsitem.headline: Japan's slow recovery clouds steelmakers profits.

text.p: Japanese steelmakers posted mixed half-year earnings on Friday, with profits hindered by the nation's feeble economic recovery as well as high steel inventory levels.

Steelmakers are considered a bellwether for Japan's industrial health and their earnings results showed that the economy is still troubled. The gains were due mainly to some painful cost-cutting and weakness in the yen, which helped export sales.
Industry leader Nippon Steel Corp said it suffered a 3.2 percent drop in its parent current profit to 28.45 billion yen ($254 million) in the six months to September 30.
For the full year, the steel giant sees profits growing 23.7 percent to 80 billion yen ($714 million). Current profit is pre-tax profit including losses and gains on investments.
"Our steel output remained low...and the steel product market is sluggish. We are still in a severe business environment," Nippon Steel said in a statement.
Nippon Steel, whose subsidiaries also suffered slumping business in areas such as chemicals and semiconductors, forecast a net loss of 20 billion yen ($178 million) for the year on a group basis.
Kobe Steel Ltd and Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd also posted lower half-year profits.

Kobe Steel's half-year profit sagged 16.3 percent to 11.13 billion yen ($99.3 million) from a year earlier. It also forecast an 83.4 percent plunge in full-year profit to 25 billion yen ($223 million).
The one-two punch of lower steel prices and falling chip prices hit Kobe Steel's mainstream business as well as electronics machinery operations.
"The profit decline came because of the difficult steel market condition," a company official said.

Steel stocks have piled up due to oversupply, as makers had expected greater demand for steel construction materials due to reconstruction following the massive earthquake in Kobe in January last year and a recovery in the overall economy.
The outlook for the market is not rosy.

Steelmakers see product prices remaining at their current low levels for the rest of this fiscal year, and predict nationwide crude steel output of around 98 million tonnes for the full year, down from 100 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Sumitomo Metal Industries posted a 10.9 percent drop in its interim profit to 7.32 billion yen ($65.3 million), but forecast an 8.6 percent rise in profit to 22 billion yen ($196 million) in 1996/97.
"The sluggish steel market and higher prices for material put the whole steel industry in a severe situation," the company said in a statement.
Two other steelmakers -- NKK Corp and Kawasaki Steel Corp -- reported healthy profit increases.

NKK announced a 60.7 percent jump in half-year current profit to 9.68 billion yen ($86.4 million) and forecast a 31.9 percent rise in full-year profit to 40 billion yen ($357 million), saying that successful cost-cutting efforts would offset slumping sales.

Kawasaki Steel also enjoyed a 34.1 percent profit increase for the first half of the year to 8.31 billion yen ($74.1 million) and saw a 26.3 percent rise in its full year profit to 21 billion yen ($187 million).
The company said the yen 's recent retreat pushed up steel export prices and recent restructuring efforts also helped boost interim profits. ($1=112 yen)
